display.title: Episode 154: On the Road, Chapter 2 (Yud-Tes Kislev)
display.summary_short: A Chanukah mission of Ahavas Yisroel, saying thank you to Mommy, and the Maggid of Mezritch explains why his real home is 'so very different'.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the week of Yud-Tes Kislev, with Chanukah a week away. Uncle Yossi gives Tzivos Hashem members a Chanukah mission: Ahavas Yisroel, inviting a friend or relative who knows little about Chanukah to share in lighting the menorah. After the Hakochainik march and the sponsor, Mitzvah Time reviews everything learned about honoring parents, including that parents are Hashem's partners, and a caller wins by explaining that good behavior is the greatest honor. The new mitzvah is hakaras hatov: eat what Mommy prepares and, after bentching, thank her for the meal. A six-year-old yeshiva student leads the Shema. The story concludes: the Maggid of Mezritch reads the Baal Shem Tov's letter and answers Reb Chaim's question about his bare cabin: 'At home it is so very different.' This world is only a temporary lodging; his real home is in Gan Eden, and he spends his life furnishing it with Torah and mitzvos. Uncle Yossi explains that the story was chosen because Thursday is Yud-Tes Kislev, the Maggid's yahrzeit, and ends with news of the Chanukah issue of the Moshiach Times.
display.lesson: This world is a place to shop for our real home: every mitzvah and every bit of Torah furnishes it.
